candidates.location_hint: the persistent status message container that updates when loading or ready
candidates.why: atomic mode forces assistive technology to re-read the entire container on every update, which could be noisy or redundant if other content is added later.

candidates.location_hint: the persistent error message container that conditionally shows text
candidates.why: keeping an alert region mounted but empty may cause some screen readers to announce the role repeatedly or ignore it until content appears, warranting a cross-AT check.

candidates.location_hint: the individual transaction rows inside the list
candidates.why: screen readers may announce the values in a confusing order or without context, so verifying if explicit labels or a definition list would clarify the data relationship is worthwhile.

candidates.location_hint: the interactive retry control in the panel header
candidates.why: offset outlines can sometimes clip or appear detached on certain browsers or assistive technologies, so confirming the visual boundary is clear and does not overlap adjacent elements is recommended.

candidates.location_hint: the status message text and the error message text
candidates.why: the color choices may sit near contrast thresholds on certain displays or for users with low vision, making a ratio verification prudent.

candidates.location_hint: the container wrapping the transaction items
candidates.why: explicitly setting a list role on a native list element can sometimes confuse assistive technology if the implicit semantics are already correct, so checking for double-announcement or role confusion is advised.
